title: Truck full of lab monkeys carrying COVID, herpes & hepatitis C crashes in Mississippi — most escape and authorities are scrambling to cover it up
content:
This story is absolutely insane and the fact that it's barely getting mainstream coverage should tell you everything.

October 28, 2025. A truck hauling rhesus monkeys from Tulane University — one of the biggest biomedical research institutions in the country — crashes on I-59 in Jasper County, Mississippi. Monkeys escape. The Jasper County Sheriff's Department immediately warns the public that these animals are aggressive and carry hepatitis C, herpes, AND COVID-19. Three separate deadly pathogens. In monkeys. Loose on a highway in rural Mississippi.

And what happens next? Tulane swoops in within HOURS and releases a carefully worded statement saying the primates 'aren't infectious.' Just like that. No independent verification. No CDC involvement announced. No public health quarantine zone. Just 'trust us, they're fine.' Does that sound like transparency to you?

Think about this: the sheriff's department said the DRIVER himself told law enforcement the monkeys were dangerous and posed a direct threat to humans. This is the guy literally transporting them. He would know what he's hauling. But suddenly Tulane says nah, nothing to worry about, and everyone's supposed to move on?

The department initially said they 'destroyed' all but one of the escapees, then had to walk that back to THREE still missing once Tulane people showed up. So nobody even knew how many monkeys were on the truck? What kind of operation is this? What else are they transporting on public highways that we don't know about?

Rhesus monkeys are literally the number one primate used in infectious disease research. They are used specifically BECAUSE they can carry human-transmissible diseases. Tulane has entire programs studying exactly these pathogens in these exact animals. But this particular batch? Oh they're totally clean. Sure.

I'm not saying panic. I'm saying ask questions. Why are research primates being moved on public interstates? Why did the official story change three times in 24 hours? And why is nobody in the media pushing back on Tulane's blanket denial?

Something doesn't add up.
topic: Did monkeys carrying COVID-19, herpes, and hepatitis C escape after a truck crash in Mississippi?

title: Exposed: Pineapple juice contains an enzyme that DESTROYS cancer cells — and the pharma industry has known for decades
content:
Before you scroll past this, just hear me out. I spent the last three months going down this rabbit hole after my cousin was diagnosed with early-stage leukemia and I started looking into everything.

Pineapple contains an enzyme called bromelain. It's been studied since the 1970s. There are peer-reviewed papers showing that bromelain has direct cytotoxic effects on cancer cells — meaning it literally breaks them apart. One study from the journal Planta Medica found that bromelain outperformed 5-fluorouracil (a common chemo drug) in an animal tumor model. Let that sink in. A natural fruit enzyme outperformed chemotherapy.

So why isn't this front-page news? Follow the money. The global oncology drug market is worth over $200 BILLION per year. You think Pfizer and Roche want you to know that something you can buy for $3 at the grocery store might fight cancer? They'd lose everything.

I'm not saying throw away your doctor's advice overnight. But I AM saying the medical establishment has a financial incentive to suppress natural alternatives. There are clinics in Mexico and Germany that use bromelain-based protocols alongside other natural treatments, and the recovery stories coming out of those places are incredible.

My cousin started drinking fresh pineapple juice daily — not the processed stuff, FRESH — along with turmeric and ginger. His next blood panel showed improvement. Coincidence? Maybe. But maybe not.

The indigenous peoples of South America have used pineapple medicinally for centuries. We act like modern Western medicine invented healing, but nature had the answers long before Big Pharma started patenting molecules.

Do your own research. Look into bromelain studies yourself. The information is out there if you're willing to look past what the mainstream wants you to believe. They can't patent a pineapple, and that's exactly why they'll never tell you the truth.

title: No, your kid isn't "mandated" to get 72 shots. Here's what the CDC schedule actually says.
content:
Seeing the '72 injections' claim making the rounds again, so let me break this down because I actually sat down and counted every line on the CDC immunization schedule.

First, the word "mandated." The CDC does not and cannot mandate anything. They RECOMMEND vaccines. Vaccine requirements are set at the STATE level for school entry, and every single state offers medical exemptions. Most offer religious or philosophical exemptions too. Nobody is holding your kid down because the CDC said so.

Second, where does "72" even come from? The CDC schedule from birth through age 18 recommends approximately 50 doses of 17 different vaccines. You can get to a higher number if you count each antigen in a combination vaccine separately — like counting the MMR as three separate shots instead of one injection — but that's not how it works in practice. Your kid gets ONE needle for MMR, not three. Some people also fold in the annual flu shot for every year of childhood and count each one, or add in COVID boosters at maximum frequency, to inflate the number.

The actual number of discrete injections a child receives is well under 72. Combination vaccines like Pediarix (DTaP + IPV + Hep B in one shot) significantly reduce the needle count.

I get that the schedule looks intimidating if you're a new parent — I was nervous too. But inflating the numbers and calling recommendations "mandates" isn't honest criticism, it's fearmongering. If you have real concerns, talk to your pediatrician about the actual schedule, not a meme number from a political speech.

The real conversation about vaccine policy deserves real numbers, not made-up ones.
topic: Are US children mandated to receive 72 vaccine injections under the CDC schedule?

title: No, Assam did NOT ban inter-religious land sales — here's what the policy actually says
content:
Seeing a ton of posts claiming that the Assam government has outright banned land sales between Hindus and Muslims. This is misleading and I'm tired of watching people run with half-truths.

Here's what actually happened: The Assam cabinet approved a new Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to REGULATE inter-religious land transfers. Not ban. Regulate. There's a massive difference.

Under the new SOP, if you want to buy or sell land to someone of a different religion, the application goes through the District Commissioner, then to the Revenue Department. The Special Branch of the Assam Police reviews the case to check for fraud, coercion, illegality, verifies the source of funds against tax returns, and assesses whether the sale could disturb social harmony in the area. After that scrutiny, the District Commissioner makes the final call — approve or reject.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma himself explained this during his briefing. He said land transfers between different religious groups in a sensitive state like Assam need to be handled "very, very carefully." At NO point did he say transactions are banned. He literally outlined the approval process step by step.

The same rules apply to NGOs from outside Assam seeking land for schools or hospitals, while recognized local NGOs are exempt.

Is the process more bureaucratic now? Sure. Could it be used to slow things down in practice? That's a fair debate to have. But claiming there's an outright BAN is factually wrong and just fuels outrage for clicks. The policy streamlines the process and adds oversight — it doesn't eliminate the right to transact.

Stop sharing screenshots without reading the actual policy. This is exactly how misinformation spreads.

title: PSA: No, pineapple juice does NOT cure blood cancer. Stop sharing that garbage before someone skips chemo.
content:
I keep seeing this post shared on Facebook, TikTok, and now here claiming pineapple juice is some miracle cure for blood cancer. My aunt has CLL (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and someone in her church group literally told her to stop treatment and drink pineapple juice instead. I am so tired of this.

Let me break this down:

1) The claim usually references bromelain, an enzyme in pineapple. Yes, there are a handful of in-vitro studies (meaning in a petri dish, not in a human body) where bromelain showed some anti-tumor properties. But guess what? Bleach kills cancer cells in a petri dish too. That doesn't make it medicine.

2) There is literally ZERO clinical trial evidence that pineapple juice treats any form of cancer in living humans. None. The National Cancer Institute does not list it as a treatment. No oncologist on earth is prescribing Dole cans.

3) AFP Fact Check investigated this specific claim and spoke with actual oncologists and cancer researchers. Dr. Ian Olver, a former CEO of the Cancer Council Australia, called the claim 'completely unfounded.' Multiple hematologists confirmed there is no mechanism by which drinking pineapple juice could eliminate malignant blood cells.

4) The viral posts often claim pineapple is '10,000 times stronger than chemo.' This number is completely fabricated. It doesn't come from any study, anywhere, ever.

The real danger here isn't just misinformation — it's that vulnerable people with treatable cancers might delay or refuse evidence-based treatment. Blood cancers like leukemia and lymphoma have seen massive improvements in survival rates thanks to modern medicine. Telling someone to swap that for fruit juice is genuinely dangerous.

If you see someone sharing this, please push back. Lives could literally depend on it.
topic: Can pineapple juice cure blood cancer?

The information war is just as important as what's happening on the ground. Don't let legacy media be your only source. Seek out what they're hiding from you. The truth is always in what they refuse to show.
topic: Does a viral video show people rallying in support of the Iranian government during the recent protests?

title: They're doing it again — Philippines quietly prepping for Nipah virus lockdowns and nobody's paying attention
content:
I know people are going to call me paranoid but hear me out. A few days ago reports started circulating that Philippine authorities are considering lockdowns and strict movement restrictions because of Nipah virus. And what happened? The DOH immediately comes out to "reassure" everyone that there's nothing to worry about, no cases, no restrictions planned.

Sound familiar? Because that's EXACTLY what they said in January 2020 about COVID. "No need to panic." "We have it under control." "No travel restrictions necessary." We all know how that turned out.

Here's what's actually happening: Nipah virus has been spreading in India, the fatality rate is anywhere from 40-75%, and there is NO vaccine. Let that sink in. This makes COVID look like a cold. The DOH says they have "surveillance protocols" at airports — the same airports that let COVID walk right in three years ago.

Think about the timeline. The post about potential lockdowns gets massive engagement — over 2,400 reactions, 1,200 comments — because regular people on the ground are hearing things. Then within days the government rushes to deny everything and media outlets start running "fact checks" to suppress the conversation. They're not fact-checking, they're narrative-controlling.

Why would the Bureau of Quarantine specifically mention they're ensuring "preparedness of frontliners at airports and seaports" if there's truly nothing to worry about? Why coordinate with "other health partners" over a virus that supposedly isn't even here? You don't mobilize resources for a non-threat.

I'm not saying go buy 6 months of rice tomorrow. But I AM saying start paying attention to what they do, not what they say. Stock up on essentials quietly. The people who prepared early for COVID were called crazy too — until they weren't.

Remember: the government's job isn't to inform you. It's to prevent panic until they're ready to act.
topic: Are Philippine government authorities preparing for a lockdown due to a potential Nipah virus outbreak?

title: They gave every newborn in America a Hep B shot for 30+ years and it was NEVER properly tested. Let that sink in.
content:
So I went down a rabbit hole after the ACIP vote in December and what I found is genuinely disturbing.

Mark Blaxill presented evidence at the actual CDC advisory committee meeting showing that the hepatitis B vaccine given to newborns was never adequately tested in proper randomized, placebo-controlled trials — you know, the gold standard we supposedly require before injecting something into a hours-old baby. And nobody on the panel could refute it.

Think about that. Since 1991, every baby born in an American hospital got this shot within 12 hours of birth. Exposed to a pharmaceutical product that didn't go through the rigorous testing they tell us EVERY vaccine goes through. For over THREE DECADES.

And here's the kicker — when the committee finally voted 8-3 to pull back the universal recommendation, the entire medical establishment lost its mind. The AAP immediately issued statements trying to discredit the decision. Why? If the vaccine is so safe and so necessary, why are they terrified of parents simply having a conversation with their doctor about it?

The new recommendation is just "shared clinical decision-making" — literally just saying parents should be able to discuss it with their pediatrician. That's it. And they're acting like it's the end of the world.

Let's also talk about why a newborn needs a vaccine for a disease primarily spread through sexual contact and IV drug use. Your 6-pound baby is not at risk for hepatitis B if the mother tested negative. Period. The risk-based approach makes infinitely more sense than jabbing every single infant on day one.

The fact that it took 33 years for anyone on these panels to even question the evidence base tells you everything you need to know about how captured these institutions are. They don't review evidence — they rubber stamp whatever pharma puts in front of them.

Do your own research. Actually read what was presented at that meeting. The house of cards is falling.
topic: Were hepatitis B vaccines for infants sufficiently tested in randomized, placebo-controlled trials?

title: The government just quietly admitted sunbeds are AS DANGEROUS AS SMOKING and nobody is talking about it
content:
I can't believe this isn't getting more attention. The UK Department of Health just came out and said it plainly: sunbeds are as dangerous as smoking. This isn't some fringe theory — it's literally from the World Health Organization. Both are classified in the SAME cancer category. Group 1 carcinogens. Same box as asbestos and plutonium.

Let that sink in. Every tanning salon in your town is basically running a cancer booth and we just... let it happen? The Health Secretary Wes Streeting posted about it. NHS England shared it. It's on gov.uk. This is as official as it gets.

And yet the tanning industry is barely regulated compared to tobacco. No graphic warnings on the door. No age verification in half the places. No massive tax to discourage use. Why? Because the beauty industry lobby is absolutely massive and nobody wants to touch it. Follow the money.

I have a friend who used sunbeds 2-3 times a week in her twenties and got melanoma at 34. Her dermatologist told her it was almost certainly the sunbeds. She had no family history. And the stats back this up — the WHO found that using a sunbed before age 35 increases your melanoma risk by 59%. FIFTY-NINE PERCENT. That's not a rounding error.

What really gets me is that people will absolutely roast you for smoking but then go hop in a tanning bed every week like it's a spa day. The cognitive dissonance is unreal. The WHO literally put them in the same danger category and people are still acting like it's fine because "it's just a tan."

We banned smoking in public spaces. We put warnings on cigarette packs. We taxed them into oblivion. If sunbeds are genuinely in the same WHO category, why aren't we treating them the same way? Something doesn't add up and I think the answer is that billion-dollar industries don't regulate themselves.

Wake up people. Your "healthy glow" might be killing you just as fast as a pack of Marlboros.
topic: Are sunbeds as dangerous as smoking?

title: They're really going to start charging our pensioners £5 just to see a doctor — and the media is barely covering it
content:
I don't even know where to start with this. My mum sent me the video of Starmer literally saying, in his own words, that starting this October anyone over 60 will be charged £5 just to see their GP. Five quid every single time you need to see a doctor. For pensioners. People who built this country.

And before someone says "oh it's just a fiver" — think about it. My gran sees her GP probably twice a month for her blood pressure and her arthritis. That's £120 a year she doesn't have. She's on state pension, barely keeping the heating on as it is. Multiply that across every pensioner in the country and you start to see what this really is: a stealth tax on the elderly to plug the holes in a system they already paid into their entire working lives.

What really gets me is they snuck this out with zero fanfare. No debate in Parliament. No manifesto commitment. Just a quiet little announcement hoping nobody would notice. And the mainstream media? Crickets. Absolute crickets. The BBC hasn't said a word. Almost like they were told not to.

This is how the privatisation of the NHS starts, people. Not with a big dramatic sell-off, but with little charges here and there. £5 for the GP today. £10 for A&E tomorrow. Before you know it we're living in America and choosing between food and healthcare.

Remember when they promised the NHS would always be free at the point of use? Remember when Labour was supposed to be the party that protects it? Starmer has completely sold out. First the winter fuel allowance, now this. They're systematically stripping support from the generation that needs it most.

Share the video before they scrub it from everywhere. People need to know what's coming. Write to your MP. This cannot stand.
topic: Has the UK government announced that over-60s will be charged £5 to see their GP?

title: RFK Jr. confirmed under oath that ANYONE can still get the COVID booster — the media is lying about "restrictions" to create panic
content:
Did anyone else actually watch the Senate hearing on Sept 4 or does everyone just read headlines?

Sen. Warren tried to trap RFK Jr. with a gotcha question about vaccine availability and he didn't flinch. He said clearly: "Anybody can get the booster." The HHS spokeswoman confirmed it too — the COVID vaccine remains available for anyone who chooses it in consultation with their healthcare provider.

So why is every mainstream outlet running stories about how vaccines are "harder to get"? Because they're furious that Kennedy is finally bringing accountability to a system that pushed these shots on healthy 6-month-olds with zero long-term safety data.

Here's what actually happened: the FDA made the approval more targeted this season — 65+ and people with health conditions get priority. That's called RESPONSIBLE MEDICINE. Not everyone needs a booster every single year. That was always pharma marketing, not science.

The media is spinning "you might need to talk to your doctor first" as some kind of crisis. Since when is consulting your healthcare provider before getting a medical intervention a BAD thing? That's literally how every other medication works. The walk-in-and-get-jabbed-at-CVS model was the anomaly, not the norm.

And notice how they keep bringing up ACIP like it's some sacred institution. Kennedy reformed a committee that had massive conflicts of interest with pharmaceutical companies. He's putting in fresh voices and suddenly that's "controversial." It's only controversial if you liked the revolving door between regulators and pharma.

Even Cassidy's complaints were about bureaucratic hiccups during a transition period, not some permanent denial of access. The system is being restructured to be more responsible.

The bottom line is if you want the booster, you can get it. Kennedy said it, HHS confirmed it. The rest is media spin designed to undermine the one person in government actually questioning whether we need to inject every man, woman, and child annually with a product that's been on the market for 4 years.
topic: Can anybody get the COVID-19 booster vaccine this fall season?

title: Congress just voted to keep the vehicle kill switch mandate alive — they literally want the ability to strand you on command
content:
I cannot believe more people aren't talking about this. In January, Congress had a chance to KILL the vehicle kill switch mandate — an amendment that would've stopped this dystopian nightmare in its tracks — and they voted it down. They actively chose to keep it.

For those who don't know, buried deep in the 2021 infrastructure bill (page 404, look it up) is a provision requiring ALL new vehicles to have technology that can 'prevent or limit motor vehicle operation.' Read that again. They're requiring technology that can SHUT YOUR CAR DOWN.

They'll tell you it's about drunk driving. Sure. That's always how it starts. 'It's for safety.' 'Think of the children.' Meanwhile they're building the infrastructure to remotely disable any vehicle they want. You think a system designed to prevent a car from operating CAN'T be accessed remotely? In 2026? When everything is connected to the internet?

NHTSA is actively researching touch sensors for steering wheels and ignition systems that read your biometrics. How long before 'impaired driving' gets redefined to include whatever they want? Driving to a protest? 'Erratic behavior detected.' Missed a tax payment? 'Vehicle operation limited.'

Even DeSantis called it straight out of 1984, and he's right. The fact that both parties voted for this in 2021 tells you everything you need to know. This isn't left vs right — this is the government vs YOU.

And the kicker? They gave NHTSA a deadline of November 2024 to draft the rules, which they conveniently missed. So now it's happening behind closed doors with zero public input. No transparency. No accountability.

They don't want you to own your car. They want you to have a vehicle they can control. Wake up people. Share this before it gets buried.
topic: Did the U.S. Congress pass a bill in January 2026 allowing the government to remotely shut down vehicles?

title: WATCH: Residents physically fight back government goons who came to destroy the Aravalli Hills — this is what resistance looks like 🔥
content:
This video is absolutely insane and the mainstream media is completely ignoring it. Government officials showed up to start carving up the Aravalli Hills — you know, the ancient mountain range that's basically the lungs of northern India — and the local residents said absolutely NOT.

You can see in the footage: people armed with whatever they could grab, sticks, stones, standing their ground against a full police deployment firing tear gas at them. These aren't 'rioters' — these are farmers, families, people who have lived alongside these hills for generations. And the government sends POLICE against them? For what? For trying to protect an ecosystem that's been around for millions of years?

This all kicked off after the Supreme Court's ruling on November 20, 2025, where they accepted the Environment Ministry's shady new definition of the Aravalli Hills and Ranges. Basically they just redrew the boundaries so developers and mining interests could move in on areas that were previously protected. The protests have been building for weeks and clearly the government thought they could just bulldoze their way through — literally.

But the people aren't having it. 40+ officials reportedly injured because they underestimated how much these communities care about their land. Good. Maybe next time they'll think twice before showing up with bulldozers and tear gas.

The fact that this isn't front page news on every channel tells you everything about whose side the media is on. They'll cover celebrity weddings for 48 hours straight but won't show you citizens being tear-gassed for defending mountains. Share this everywhere because apparently we have to be our own media now. The Aravalli belongs to the people, not to corporations and corrupt bureaucrats.

This is what happens when you push people too far. Respect.
topic: Does the viral video show a clash between residents and government officials during a protest over the Aravalli Hills?
